reasons: Both answers cover the same core plan: validate and normalize complaints, check the pipeline, explain data drift and per-class effects, then run a paired, blind-labeled comparison on fresh data with shadow mode. B goes further on complaint validity: it audits a sample of complaints and groups them by category pair. It also explicitly reweights by the production class mix and gives a pre-agreed decision table, which maps more directly onto rubric items 2-4. A is equally sound but a bit less concrete on the final decision criteria.

A: Claims that when one predicted category spikes sharply, 'the label is never correct', an overstated and unclear assertion
B: Suggests that 90% inter-annotator agreement puts an 87 vs 91% difference in the noise zone. That is overstated for a paired comparison of both models against the same labels
